established-l1 pinned the battery and targeted set to bor cb3d19c5f690 and 280514fa9fb7 on polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com. The verifier saw ebcfea01452d and a863b8e5cce1 answer within the same seconds, and a critic query on 2026-11-26 got bor/f2a2d63e69f6/v2.11.1-private/linux-amd64/go1.26.10. At least five private commits answer behind one endpoint and three of them have no pinned run in any cycle.

established-l1 records that the C-Chain now accepts a block before executing it (SAE executor, saexec/execution.go:293-470) and that latest is the last accepted block while safe and finalized lag six blocks. Nobody asked what eth_call at latest executes against under SAE, or whether a transaction in an accepted block can execute differently from the checks made at acceptance. Every Avalanche eth_call result since the switch, the battery included, may speak for a state that differs from the one blocks are executed on. Avalanche also has the thinnest mined swap evidence of all networks (59 swaps in OPCODES.md Check 3, 19,251 replayed in cycle 23).

The erigon v3.8.1 per-frame SLOAD cache is keyed by an IntraBlockState read stamp whose definition no unit found. The research lead and the verifier lead ask the same question. The probe in ethereum-reference covered nested writes, a reverted nested write and a delegatecall write, but the stamp source is unread, so the clearance rests on one probe shape.
L-985 is inconclusive: the Zora census did not finish and the Base and World Chain endpoints refused wide log ranges, so the census windows for those three networks did not grow this cycle.

The BNB Smart Chain traced replay stopped at 14,274 transactions (L-1024) and bsc-rpc.publicnode.com now returns a Cloudflare challenge to this session, so the reth-bsc build behind it was not reached by any rerun this cycle.

titles: Does the PoolManager on any of the 21 networks hold at least 2^96 units of a token, so that an ordinary account could borrow it with take and drive the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp
Attacker pool with its own token as currency0
duplicates.note: Contradiction with the threat model. The lead assumes the amount must be borrowed from the PoolManager. An ordinary account can mint any amount of its own token, deploy it at an address below a real token so it sorts as currency0, and swap it into its own hookless pool against that real token at a price near MAX_SQRT_PRICE. amount * sqrtPX96 then overflows at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:42-43 for an amount above about 2^96, while the int128 casts at src/libraries/Pool.sol:453-458 still allow amounts up to 2^127. A wrong result there pays out the real token, which belongs to other pools. The borrowing precondition is not needed, and the lead should be rewritten as the lead below.

leads.question: On 8 December 2026 after 15:00 UTC (T14) and again after T15 on 15 December, which tempo release and commit does rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz report, which evm2 revision and ruint version does its Cargo.lock pin, and do the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, SHL, SHR, SAR, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE and JUMPI handlers and the jump destination kernels differ from a9d6748? Do battery.py, targeted.py, vec/ruintedges.py and script sets 1, 2 and 6 at 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 give the recorded words, and does a zero divisor still give 0 if the release moves DIV and MOD to checked_div and checked_rem?
leads.why: Tempo has one client, so an arithmetic fault in the T14 release is what the chain computes. Any account can create a pool of its own token against a pooled stablecoin and drive FullMath, UnsafeMath and SqrtPriceMath to any edge, so a wrong word could pay out other pools' funds. This carries L-1033, which no unit held in cycle 24.

leads.question: In the bor release that carries Salvador (block 98,688,600), is core/vm/mulmod_memo.go active by default, is the memo held per interpreter, per BlockSTM worker or per process, and does it return the right word when two consecutive MULMOD instructions in one frame use the same modulus with different operands, when the modulus alternates between 2^256-1 and a denominator across consecutive mulDiv calls (FullMath.mulDiv uses 2^256-1 at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and the denominator at :48, and mulDivRoundingUp adds a third at :112), when z aliases the modulus, and when two BlockSTM workers run MULMOD with different moduli at the same time? Add those sequences to targeted.py and run them pinned to the post-fork build on every Polygon endpoint.
leads.why: established-l1 read the memo on develop and found it keyed on the full modulus, but it is on every mulDiv call of every swap, and the Salvador release is untagged. A memo that serves a stale reciprocal across workers would change pool amounts on the block producers themselves, and eth_call runs one worker only. Merge with L-1032 for the Jenner half.

leads.question: HyperEVM's validator has never executed an exact-output swap, a donate, clear, settleFor or an ERC-6909 transfer on the PoolManager (F-120). The HyperEVM testnet endpoint rpc.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/evm answers chain id 0x3e6 and 'hyperliquid evm Testnet' (critic query 2026-11-26) and has no code at the mainnet PoolManager address. Does any contract on the testnet carry a runtime whose masked hash equals fe1b801727eb (the PoolManager build), found through Initialize logs (topic 0xdd466e674ea557f56295e2d0218a125ea4b4f0f6f3307b95f85e6110838d6438) over the testnet history? If so, which of those branch sides did its mined transactions execute, do they replay to the source with pyevm_cov.py, and does the testnet validator run the mainnet release?
leads.why: Mined evidence from the closed validator is the only check that reaches it, and mainnet users have left exact-output swaps untested in the whole history. An exact-output fault in the validator would pay any account that sends such a swap. Testnet blocks already mined by others give producer evidence without sending a transaction.

leads.question: theme-storage-key-mapping reports that reth v2.11.0 commits a speculative prewarm result without re-running the transaction when its recorded reads still match. Does the tempo v1.19.1 node (and the T14 release), base v1.5.6 and op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 contain the same commit-without-rerun path in block building or block validation? For each, does the recorded read set include TLOAD-free inputs such as the PoolManager's native balance (SELFBALANCE at src/types/Currency.sol:92), the balanceOf answer of a token whose balance an earlier transaction of the block changed, code of an account created earlier in the block, and the original slot value used for SSTORE gas?
leads.why: Transfer from Ethereum, where reth is a minority client and a wrong commit only forks that client off. On Tempo the node is the only client, so a missed read would become the canonical state. An account that sends two transactions into one block could then have settle (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360) credit a balance rise measured on stale state.

leads.question: For a hookless pool whose currency0 is a token the attacker minted at an address below a real currency1, with sqrtPriceX96 between 2^158 and MAX_SQRT_PRICE and an exact-input zeroForOne amount between 2^97 and 2^127, which path does getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp take (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:41-52), and do eth_call on all 21 networks (token double by state override), pyevm.py and Monad's compiled harness at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 give the same price and amounts? Which of these inputs did any mined MegaETH, HyperEVM or Monad transaction execute?
leads.why: This corrects the 2^96 lead: the amount comes from the attacker's own token, so the fallback at :45 and :52 is reachable today by any account, and a wrong price there pays out the real token side. Producer evidence for this site is zero on all three closed or compiled producers.

leads.question: The MegaETH testnet endpoints carrot.megaeth.com/rpc and timothy.megaeth.com/rpc answer chain id 0x18c7 and the same replica build as mainnet, mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42 (critic query 2026-11-26). Is a PoolManager build (masked hash fe1b801727eb) deployed there, and do its mined transactions cover the branch sides F-118 lists as never executed on mainnet (donate, clear, settleFor, ERC-6909 transfer and approve, the mulDiv 512-bit copies, the SqrtPriceMath fallback)? Does the testnet sequencer run the same JIT release as mainnet?
leads.why: The mainnet producer is closed and its never-executed sides are reachable by any account. Testnet blocks are producer evidence that exists without sending a transaction.

leads.question: Under the SAE executor of avalanchego 1.15.3, what state does eth_call at latest, at safe and at a block number run against: the last accepted block before its execution, or the last settled state? Can a transaction pass the checks made at acceptance and then execute with a different result, and can execution skip, fail or reorder a transaction inside an accepted block in a way that leaves a PoolManager unlock half applied? Read saexec and the RPC backend at commit 983815fd.
leads.why: Every Avalanche eth_call result, the battery included, was assumed to speak for block execution. With acceptance separated from execution that assumption is untested, and a transaction whose execution differs from what was checked at acceptance is the kind of path an ordinary account could aim at a victim's withdrawal.

leads.question: Which Monad release do mainnet validators run on the day of the next unit (the release page listed v0.16.5 while rpc.monad.xyz answered Monad/0.16.7 on 2026-11-26), and if any validator moved to v0.16.6 or later, do the compiled harness of cycle 23 at that release and swaps.py and replay.py on blocks after the move give the recorded results? Do the release notes since v0.16.7 change vm.cpp, the x86 emitter or the 256 bit library?
leads.why: Monad blocks run compiled code that eth_call never uses. A new emitter fault on validators would change pool state for every swap that reaches the compiled path. Carries L-613.

leads.question: Do rpc.mainnet.arc.io and arc.drpc.org still report the commits 37812c61 and 8e8edb7a, and do the F-125 probes (native take to address(0), to a blocklisted account, to an account destroyed earlier in the transaction, and with amount 0) and the battery give the recorded answers at today's block? leads.question: Rerun battery.py and targeted.py on polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com with run_pin.py, keeping only answers bracketed by the same build string, until each of f2a2d63e69f6, ebcfea01452d, a863b8e5cce1, cb3d19c5f690 and 280514fa9fb7 has a full run. Does any of them answer differently?

leads.question: On Celo and X Layer, how far does the unsafe head run ahead of safe at the public endpoints, which parties can replace those blocks (sequencer, batcher, an L1 reorg, X Layer's risk filter on L1 deposits), and does forno's op-geth backend serve blocks that the canonical chain later replaced?
leads.why: L6 for these two networks was skipped this cycle. It decides whether a payment shown on public RPC can be undone after a payout, which matters for bridges and fast withdrawals that hold PoolManager claims.

leads.question: Run the jdtest inputs of cycles/024/ethereum-reference.work through the Nethermind 2.2.2 jump destination kernels (Vector512 with AVX-512 VBMI, Vector256, SSSE3, AdvSimd) and the erigon v3.8.1 NEON kernel, each forced by build flags or a software model as cycle 20 did for evm2, and compare with the scalar bitmap on the PoolManager runtime and its prefix and suffix cuts.
leads.why: A kernel that rejects a valid JUMPDEST in the PoolManager on one CPU family would make that client fail every swap and fork off. It merges the two low and medium leads of ethereum-reference and stays below high because both are minority clients.

leads.question: Find IntraBlockState.ReadStamp in erigon v3.8.1 (search the whole execution/ and core/ trees and the generated code, beyond the six files the verifier listed). Does the stamp change on every journalled SetState in any frame, on every RevertToSnapshot, and on SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE2 into an address that had storage?
leads.why: A stale per-frame SLOAD would change a PoolManager read after a hook writes and reverts in a nested frame. It is a minority client, so the effect is a fork of that client, and the probe already passed on one shape.

leads.question: F-020 stays plausible. Does Hyperliquid documentation or the nanoreth source state whether the validator checks any authorization for the sender of a system transaction, and whether HyperCore can emit a system transaction whose sender is an EVM contract that never linked a token, such as 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F?
leads.why: That one fact settles F-020. It is operator level, so it stays out of scope, but it decides whether the PoolManager's balances depend on the validator set alone.
